Mthatha card scammers

By: Tarryn Crossman | Paid

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
We have a lot of CCTV footage of these card scammers operating and of the previous FNB sting operation.
We also have footage of them going to a car and starting to withdraw cash in the car using a machine, which Willem can explain









Summary:
It is a city in the heart of the wild coast, a thoroughfare for tourists visiting a part of our country rich in history - Mandela's birth home - and Km's of pristine, untouched beaches and wild adventures. It's the last stop for food and fuel before tourists go off the beaten track.
It is also the most dangerous city in the Eastern Cape and the 6th most dangerous city in South Africa, where a person is likely to be murdered.
And the most vulnerable - the unsuspecting tourist. The scam is foolproof.
The tourist's car is spotted, a fake roadblock is set up, and a guy wearing a reflective vest stops them.
They are told that there is a problem ahead and they will have to be detoured to a toll road, but they will need cash. This is the last place to draw from an ATM. The tourists are boxed in from the front and the back and told the front car would escort them to the ATM.
It is here that their pins are copied, and the scammers are free to withdraw what they like.
It's a perfect crime because, by the time they realise they have been scammed, they want to get out of SA. No one is hanging around to open a case or return to give evidence.

So how have these scammers been able to carry out the same scam for so many years? Where are the police?
According to these groups of locals, they are either involved or turning a blind eye.
"they are allowing these tourists into the devil's den" Zolisa Madikizela is a local who grew up here and is now fighting to get her city back from the criminals.
She has started an NGO and is recruiting private security companies to get involved and protect the tourists and the town.

Willem is the manager of the local spar. He knows this scam inside out and has been trying to get these guys arrested for years.
They have set up CCTV cameras and constantly monitor the ATM near them. They have a horn they blow when they see a scammer.
He says he will take us to the hotspots and show us a local scam within half an hour.

Martin is the head of a local private security firm. He is the one intercepting the scammers, taking them to the police and then, within a few days, they are out doing the same thing again. He has identified a scammer that has been involved for years and now has his address - speaking to him about his plan with this guy to see what we can film.

These guys are all on a WhatsApp group, constantly looking out for tourists and then escorting them through the city. I hope we get this, it is the sardine run, so Mthatha should be busy with tourists.

Contacting SAPS today again for a spokesperson

WILLEM
I raised two girls here, two daughters, and we had a happy life here.

VO1: “Here” is Mthatha in the Eastern Cape. It’s where Willem Schoeman has lived with his family, building a thriving career, for nearly 25 years. Lately, though, it’s become more hell than home

WILLEM
I never used to carry a firearm. For the last five years I have carried one every day of my life.


VO2: Rampant crime and an apparently indifferent police service has forced him into a different role in life: heading a management team one moment, tackling criminals the next.

WILLEM ON THE PHONE
Listen here …They just hit two Canadians … its two old people

Glitch and music change

VO3: The iconic Wild Coast...
PAUSE
MAP
...from the southern border of KwaZulu Natal to East London in the Eastern Cape, this jagged section of coastline is an unspoiled national treasure…
PAUSE
...with kilometres of untouched beaches and off-the-grid adventure...
PAUSE
...it attracts tourists from around the world in search of natural beauty.
PAUSE
Glitch
But to reach the Wild Coast, tourists must pass through the provinces most dangerous city: mthatha

WILLEM
once you get to Mthatha, all rules change. -
Lock your doors, close your windows, Don't trust anybody. Don't speak to anybody. Because if you interact with anybody, 90% of the time, they try to scam you out of something

VO4: Not only is Mthatha the gateway to the wild coast, but the N2 highway from Durban to Cape Town passes right through the heart of the city,
bringing unsuspecting tourists to the doorstep of criminals.

WILLEM
I will not recommend any tourist actually to travel through this town.

V05 Many residents here say the police have lost the battle against criminals. And, amidst the lawlessness, one crime thrives above most others: card scamming… where unsuspecting tourists fall victim to unrelenting and sophisticated syndicates.


VO6: For Pauline Hunter and her husband Mark, South Africa was a dream holiday destination. They arrived in 2018, driving to Durban via Mthatha.

It’s here that their dream fell apart.

PAULINE
There were a couple of guys standing on the road and all official-looking vests.
and we stopped.

VO7: It was a fake roadblock. Pauline and her husband were trapped in the scammer's web

But they weren’t the first… and nor would they be the last.

This footage was filmed by another tourist just last year…

PAUSE & LET SINK IN
It shows that nothing has changed in the scammers MO in the years following Pauline’s ordeal.

PAUSE & LET SINK IN
The scam begins in the same way Pauline described: tourists are forced to detour round a fake roadblock by scammers wearing high visibility vests.

Scammer SPEAKS OFF CAMERA:
the bridge is broken, so you have to go through a toll gate, and you need to go there to get a ticket. Follow the Mercedes

V08: After being forced into a detour, one of the scammers takes the victim to the nearest ATM where with a sleight of hand their bank cards are stolen.

PAULINE:
there were five or six of them around us, and they sort of separated us a little bit,
And I turned around and looked at my husband. He had four guys standing behind him.
That was very intimidating because we didn’t know what to do

VO9: Confused and shocked, the couple didn’t immediately block their cards, and the scammers cleaned them out

PAULINE:
They got between the two accounts that 10 000 dollars or
100,000. Rand Oh my God. 100,000 rand
We had no money. I think we had 200 rands that we had taken out in cash that morning.
We still had nearly a week of our trip to go.

VO10: It’s a story Willem has heard from countless tourists bringing valuable investment into this desperate region. After years of standing by, he’d had enough. He started a WhatsApp group and invited others in the community to help him police their besieged town.

MONTAGE OF CCTV FOOTAGE AND MESSAGES
● We with you
● Lets catch them
● I’ll send what I have


WILLEM:
We started to collect the vehicle registration numbers.
We are on high alert.
we turned the tide, and we started to fight with information.



VO11:
Amid a lack of assistance from the police, Mthatha business owners installed CCTV cameras throughout the city. The scammers were now being monitored by a community determined to fight back.
In his store alone, Willem has over 160 cameras - with ten constantly monitoring the ATMs

WILLEM:
we’ve put a loudspeaker outside. If they come here and we spot them, we make a noise, call them by name, and call them criminals. We don't shy away.

VO12: “Ruth” is among the residents putting their lives on the line to protect their businesses and the tourists. It’s not her real name, and she asked us to hide her identity for the safety of her children

RUTH ANON
I'm so against crime, and I don't like seeing people being used or vulnerable people being taken advantage of,

VO13: The group is constantly on high alert…

VO14: AFTER a message on the group saying the scammers are in action - Ruth rushes to the scene.
This dash-cam footage shows her intercepting an Israeli tourist moments before he’s scammed.

FOOTAGE OF THE SCENE
RUTH ANON:
And then I'm telling the tourists, don't put your pin. You're being scammed.
And the other guy comes from the right-hand side, and he still tells him, Put your pin, put your pin,

VO15: The scamming attempts are endless, Ruth tells us. She’s called into action every week.

Cameras mounted at the petrol station, show the tourist getting into a car… and leaving town


WILLEM
we call it the perfect crime
First of all
No case was opened
there's no blood.
Its white collar crime.

VO16: It might appear a soft crime, but it’s giving tourists yet another reason not to visit South Africa. Hardly ideal in a country hungry for the tourist dollar.


VO17: This man works in private security. For his safety, we’re calling him Victor. Another group member, he’s constantly on guard and we join him while he works backup for a joint sting operation between the community and a number of banks with branches in town.

VICTOR ANON:
How often are we seeing this happening? On a daily basis,
VO18: messages start coming in from on the group - again, card scammers are the move, targeting a Canadian couple

beat change from crime to driving miss daisy

VO19: Anne and Louis Mckenzie are both over 80. In love with South Africa, this is their fourth trip to the country.

we have a rental car and we love to tour through South Africa. The the the scenery and the vistas are spectacular.

VO20: But as they drove into Mthatha they were hit by scammers and detoured

ANNE: we were told to follow the fellow in the white car into a shopping mall,

VO21: This CCTV footage shows Anne and Louis, completely oblivious to what’s unfolding, following the scammers to the ATM. What happens next isn;t caught on camera.


ANNE AND LOUIS
I put my card in, and He said, Your card is stuck in there. You have to put another credit card in.
There was a police car parked there.
So I banged on the car's roof to get attention, and I hollered, Please, please, please.

VO22: One of Victor’s teams is FIRST ON on the scene and helps secure an arrest

MARTIN INTERVIEW
the problem we have is the police are undermanned
I think Mthata has been neglected by the government

VO23: To figure out what the police are doing to tackle the scammers we call the area’s district commissioner, Major-General Phumzile Cetyana.

Saps:
We know there is a problem and we are trying
Can’t be everywhere, mthatha is dense with people and traffic
We working on it and having meetings

VO24: While the police are making plans, tourists like Anne and Louis are not safe driving through our country - especially in hot spots like Mthatha.
They say this will probably be their last trip to South Africa.

ANNE AND LOUIS
We may be getting a little older and not quite as quick on the uptake on stuff.

couple walking off

WILLEM:The weaker the police get, the more the criminals take over.
